evidence.clarity: 1440 first screen: h1 'See your proof before we staple.', subhead 'prints zines and art books for independent artists, 25 to 500 copies, from your print-ready PDF', red 'Upload your PDF' (to staplepress.example/start) and a line under it with the two-working-day proof photo and 'Prices from $2.10 a copy'. As the illustrator I could repeat what it is and what to do inside five seconds; nothing later contradicts it.
evidence.fit: Reads as made by a press: imposition sheet with crop/registration marks, a 4-step docket (You/We, Day 0 to after proof), proofreader-mark 'galley' striking out the copy shop and big online printer terms, saddle-stapler drawing. Full-bleed limitation shown inside the hero artifact note (red marks on the cover) and in the closing line; no-permission tension resolved with 'the sheet at the top of this page is our own sample'. What it misses for this buyer: nothing engages the PDF she already has open beyond the upload link; the $2.10 ticket is static and other configs only get 'cost more'.
evidence.distinctiveness: Proof sheet as hero artifact, page-pair imposition explainer ('On your proof, page 24 sits next to page 1'), galley with del/ins proof marks and caret, technical line drawings of a nested 24-page zine and a saddle stapler, Century Schoolbook-style serif with mono slugs. Removing the logo, it is still recognisably a small press, and none of it is template icon cards or logo strips.
evidence.proof: Operable artifact in the first screen at 1440 and 390, labelled 'Sample sheet drawn for this page, not a customer's work'. Numbers are consistent (24+1=25, 6 sheets, 50 x $2.10 = $105.00). But it demonstrates imposition, i.e. how to read the proof photo, not my first doubts as a copy-shop refugee wary of upsell (will my file print well, what will my run cost). It is a dummy with page-number chips rather than anything that looks like ink on paper.
evidence.craft: No overflow at 320/390/768/1440, no console errors, axe empty, smallest text 13px. Hero at 1440 sits on a subgrid with controls aligned under the copy, sheet on the right; consistent rules, tickets and spacing down the page. Minor: at 1440 the six control buttons under the copy are dense, and the 'Reading a proof' band's left-aligned drawing and the press drawing make two similar figure-plus-prose blocks in a row.
evidence.mobile: 390: Menu button (44px) opens a panel with 5 links at 44px each; Escape closes it; tapping 'Prices' closes it and lands #prices at top=8. Headline, CTA, timing/price line and the top of the sheet all in the first 844px. Controls (stepper at y=1003, Turn over/Reset at y=1109) sit right under the sheet, so sheet and buttons fit one scroll position. All targets 44px. Only cost: status/note text sits above the controls and below the sheet, so after one scroll it is fine.
evidence.honesty: Sample label sits directly above the artifact at all widths and the slug reads 'STAPLEPRESS PROOF · SAMPLE'. Footer: 'Sheets and drawings on this page are our own samples.' Full-bleed caveat appears in the first screen note and next to the closing CTA ('No full-bleed covers yet'). Every CTA is the brief's staplepress.example/start. The ~120 artists figure is from the brief and explained ('We don't have permission to name them').
evidence.interaction: Operated at 1440/768/390: Turn over (2/23 inside), Next/Prev wrap through 6 sheets, sheet 6 inside gives the centre-spread note, +4/-4 redraw (28pp -> 7 sheets), +4 x10 caps at 64 with a written message, typed 22 draws pages 23-24 as 'blank' and explains it, 0/-8/'abc'/100/empty each give a specific written message while keeping the last valid sheet, Reset returns to 24pp sheet 1. Keyboard Enter on Turn over swaps instantly. No console errors. Small nit: on an error the note below keeps the previous sheet's text.
evidence.copy: Specific and press-literate: 'Within two working days we post a photo of your proof, straight off the press, before anything is bound', 'Struck in red: what you get now. In the margin: what you get from us.' Error microcopy is written ('A zine can't have -8 pages'). Some of it reads like a lesson to an illustrator ('24 + 1 = 25, like every side of every sheet in a 24-page zine') and the hero status line is maths before it is reassurance.
evidence.first_screen: 1440: promise, CTA, price, full-bleed caveat and an operable labelled sheet all within 900px. 390: headline, CTA, 'Within two working days... Prices from $2.10 a copy' and the sheet visible to y~780. Specific and backed by an artifact, but the artifact is a printer's dummy, so it makes the process believable more than it makes the quality believable.

problems: The hero artifact teaches imposition (how to read a proof) rather than answering the buyer's first doubts: will my PDF work and what will my run cost; she has her PDF open and the page never uses it.
Pricing is a single static ticket; anything beyond 50 x 24pp A5 black only gets 'cost more', with no indication of what happens next for her configuration.
The artifact copy ('24 + 1 = 25, like every side of every sheet') is maths-first; for an illustrator wary of being sold to it reads as a lesson before it reads as reassurance.

evidence.clarity: 1440: h1 'See your zine come off the press before we staple a single copy.', lede 'We print zines and art books in runs of 25 to 500. Upload a print-ready PDF, and within two working days we post a photo of your proof...', buttons 'Upload your PDF' and 'Check your PDF first'. What, who and next step are all clear before scrolling; the h1 is long (5 lines at 1440) but specific.
evidence.fit: Built for the buyer card's moment: 'You probably have the file open already. Drop it here' reads her PDF in the browser and fills a job ticket. The full-bleed constraint is enforced, not just stated: a bleed PDF (154x216mm with TrimBox) flags 'We can't print full-bleed covers yet', and the 'What we can't do yet' box sits beside the price. 'We publish one price, for our simplest job. Anything else, we price from your upload' directly addresses fear of upsell. Press tone through one-ink palette, job ticket, rubber stamp, ruler of run sizes.
evidence.distinctiveness: One-ink blue with screen tints, a marked-up proof sheet ('Proof 1. OK to bind?', 'dot gain ok', 'solids even'), job ticket with stamp, run-size ruler. But the structure is the familiar hero / 3 steps / tool / comparison / pricing / close sequence, and the display stack falls back to DejaVu Sans Condensed here, which looks like a default bold sans rather than a press face.
evidence.proof: Hero shows a labelled sample proof sheet (caption 'A proof from our own test zine... this sheet is ours'). The operable checker is at screen 2-3 (top at y~1456 at 1440, reachable from the hero's 'Check your PDF first', which scrolled #check to top=0). It answers her real doubt with her own file: my 24pp A5 file gave 'Ready to upload' and '$105 for the run'; 22pp gave 'Add 2 blank pages to make 24'; a spreads PDF gave 'Export single pages'; A4 16pp gave 'Priced at upload... Yours is different (16 pages, A4)'. Not in the first screen, which keeps it from 9.
evidence.craft: No overflow at any width, no console errors. Probe: one axe colour-contrast node and 2 text elements at 11px (SVG page numbers). At 1440 the checker section leaves a large empty area under the drop zone beside the tall ticket; the 5-line condensed-fallback h1 is heavy. Ticket rows, status icons and stamp states are tidy and consistent.
evidence.mobile: 390: no menu at all; nav links are display:none under 720px, leaving only the 'Upload a PDF' header button, so 'Prices' and 'Check your PDF' are reachable only by scrolling or the hero button. Hero shows h1, lede and both CTAs (55px) in the first 650px, sheet starting at y=677. Checker stacks cleanly, readout appears right under the drop zone (bleed warning shown in red). Choice buttons Black/Colour/border are 37px, Page size select 35px, under 44px.
evidence.honesty: Sample sheet is captioned right under it. Privacy is stated before the visitor drops a file ('Your file stays on your computer... sends nothing to us. You'll choose the file again on the upload page'). 'What we can't do yet' is clear without undermining. Two soft spots: the caption calls a drawn illustration 'A proof from our own test zine', and after loading a non-PDF (fake.pdf / notes.txt) the readout says it couldn't read the file while the ticket still shows the previous file's 'Ready to upload' stamp.
evidence.interaction: Operated at 1440/768/390: file input with 7 test files (A5 24pp, 22pp, bleed, spreads, A4, fake PDF, .txt), each gave a specific readout; copies 10/600/-5/empty/200, colour, A4, pages 0 and 99999999999 each produced a row note and stamp change ('Fix 1 thing before you upload' / 'Fill in the ticket' / 'Ready to upload'); price block switches between '$105 for the run' and 'Priced at upload' with the differences listed. No console errors. Weak spots: stale ticket after an unreadable file, no reset for the ticket, a huge page count yields 'Add 1 blank page to make 100000000000'.
evidence.copy: Customer-world nouns and plain verbs: 'Edit anything the PDF got wrong', 'For the runs nobody else wants to print well', 'you see your zine for the first time when the boxes arrive', 'Bring the cover art in from the edges so it sits inside a white border.' Validation microcopy is written, not defaulted. Some repetition: 'nothing is bound before you've seen the proof' appears in the lede, the steps intro and step 3.
evidence.first_screen: 1440: specific promise, two honest actions ('Upload your PDF' to the brief URL, 'Check your PDF first' to the on-page checker) and a labelled marked-up proof sheet that makes 'see your proof' concrete. No price in view. 390: h1, lede and both buttons in view, the sheet only begins at y=677 so it is barely visible.

problems: The PDF checker, the page's strongest answer to this buyer, starts around the third screen at 1440 and is not previewed in the first viewport beyond a button label.
No mobile navigation: under 720px the section links disappear with no menu, and ticket choice buttons/select are 35-37px tall.
State handling gaps in the checker: an unreadable file leaves the previous file's 'Ready to upload' ticket in place, and there is no way to clear the ticket.

reason: As the illustrator with her PDF open and a bad copy-shop experience behind her, B lets me drop my own file and tells me before I pay whether it will work (page count in fours, bleed vs. no full-bleed covers, spreads) and exactly what I'd pay or that it will be priced at upload, which answers both my doubt and my fear of upsell. A is the more polished and more distinctive page and I would be proud of it as the founder, but its artifact explains how to read a proof I don't have yet. A version of A with a tool that reads my file, or B with that checker in the first screen and a mobile menu, would change my mind.
score_preference_note: A totals higher (83 vs 79) mainly on distinctiveness, craft, mobile and interaction polish. Those count for less in a buyer's decision than whether the page answers the buyer's first doubt, and B's in-browser PDF check plus its transparent 'priced at upload' ticket do that where A's imposition explainer does not.
